physicalNotes: Radius 1.2 +/- 0.1 Jupiter radii: the Exo-REM atmospheric model Nowak et al. (2020, A&A 642, L2; arXiv:2010.04442, Section 4) fit to the flux-calibrated GRAVITY K-band spectrum (a Drift-Phoenix fit gives 1.05 +/- 0.1). A model radius, not a measured diameter: 85,790 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the dynamical mass 8.89 +/- 0.75 Jupiter masses of Lacour et al. (2021, Table 2) times Jupiter's GM 126686531.9 km^3/s^2. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

prediction.reference: Lacour et al. (2021, A&A 654, L2; arXiv:2109.10671), the RV + b and c astrometry fit, as distributed with whereistheplanet (Wang et al. 2021).

sources.period: Lacour et al. (2021, Section 5 and abstract): 1221 +/- 15 days.
sources.shape: Lacour et al. (2021, Table 2, RV + b and c astrometry): a 2.68 +/- 0.02 au at their parallax 51.44 mas, kept as the angular size 137.86 mas and placed at the Gaia DR3 distance: 2.707 au, 374.62 radii of the star's 1,080,920 km; inclination 88.95 +0.09/-0.10 degrees.
sources.argumentOfPeriapsis: Lacour et al. (2021, Table 2): omega_c 66.0 +1.8/-1.7 degrees, the planet's argument of periastron; stored as the star's, 246.0 degrees.
sources.phase: Lacour et al. (2021, Table 2): tau_c 0.724 +/- 0.006, the fraction of a period after MJD 59000 at which periastron falls: 59000 + 0.724 x 1221 = MJD 59884.0 (the paper's MJD scale, taken as BMJD_TDB).
sources.orientation: Lacour et al. (2021, A&A 654, L2; arXiv:2109.10671), Table 2, column 'RV + b and c astrometry' (posterior medians), in the orbitize! conventions of Blunt et al. (2020): Omega is the position angle of the ascending node east of celestial north and omega the planet's argument of periastron. This record stores omega in the hosted-orbit convention (the star's argument, the planet's plus 180 degrees); the node position angle is entered as published. The mapping is checked against the paper's GRAVITY astrometry in packages/astronomy/src/hostedOrbits.test.ts.
